name: Sennacherib
overview: Sennacherib was a male king of Assyria, known primarily from his role as a ruler mentioned in the biblical book of 2 Kings. His reign and actions are documented in the context of Assyrian dominance during the period recorded in Scripture. There are no additional personal notes or tribal affiliations recorded about him in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Sennacherib' means 'Sin has increased the brothers; Sin replace the [lost] brothers!' reflecting a meaning rooted in the ancient Assyrian language. He is also identified by the title 'King of Assyria,' which straightforwardly denotes his position as the sovereign ruler of the Assyrian empire, as stated in 2 Kings 18:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Sennacherib was the father of Adrammelech and Sharezer. Both sons are noted to have killed him, indicating a violent end to his reign. Additionally, Sennacherib was the son of Esarhaddon, establishing his royal lineage within the Assyrian dynasty.
scriptureSignificance: Sennacherib's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as the Assyrian king who threatened Judah during the reign of King Hezekiah. His aggressive campaigns and eventual assassination by his own sons highlight the divine judgment and sovereignty over earthly rulers. His story serves to demonstrate God's protection over His people and the downfall of those who oppose His purposes.
